## Findings ledger
- [D1.DOC2.F3] Capitalist ideology reduces rationality to “economic” rationality by identifying welfare with an economic maximum or optimum measured through maximization and minimization — dim: local_meanings — term: economic rationality — sense: a quantitative orientation toward maximizing product and minimizing costs — boundary: the regime itself determines what counts as product and cost and how each is evaluated — anchor: "In this way, rationality is reduced, directly or indirectly, to \"economic\" rationality, and the latter is defined in a purely quantitative way as maximization/minimization—maximization of a \"product\" and minimization of \"costs.\" It is obviously the regime itself that decides upon what a \"product\" is—and how this \"product\" will be evaluated—just as it decides upon what the \"costs\" will be and how much they will be." — doc: rationality — confidence: high
- [D1.DOC2.F5] “Rationalization” is also locally characterized as the capitalist extension of the tendency toward mastery through calculability and maximization/minimization — dim: local_meanings — term: rationalization — sense: a socially expansive push toward mastery using quantitative extremization — boundary: it extends beyond production into consumption, education, law, and political life, and is not merely an instrumental feature of production — anchor: "It is not only in production that such mastery is to be achieved but also, very much so, in consumption, and not only in the economy but in education, law, political life, and so on." — doc: rationality — confidence: high
- [D1.DOC2.F6] “Rational mastery” names capitalism’s core social imaginary signification: the unlimited extension of mastery through rationalization — dim: local_meanings — term: rational mastery — sense: an unlimited extension of mastery across social spheres through capitalist rationalization — boundary: the phrase is placed in quotation marks because its capitalist content is historically specific rather than universally valid — anchor: "we can characterize the core social imaginary signification of capitalism as the push toward the unlimited extension of \"rational mastery.\" Below I shall explain why I use the quotation marks." — doc: rationality — confidence: high
- [D1.DOC2.F8] In the text’s later empirical use, capitalist “rationality” denotes a restricted pursuit of increased production and reduced costs rather than a socially comprehensive or optimal reason — dim: local_meanings — term: capitalist rationality — sense: the regime’s practical orientation toward increasing a specified kind of production and reducing narrowly defined costs — boundary: environmental destruction, damaged human lives, and other social harms are excluded from the calculation — anchor: "Capitalism is the regime that aims, by every means, at increasing production—a certain kind of production, let us not forget—and, by every means, at reducing \"costs\"—costs, let us not forget either, that are defined very restrictively: neither the destruction of the environment, nor the flattening of human lives" — doc: rationality — confidence: high

sections_inspected: Specificity and Social-Historical Relativity of the Capitalist Institution
The Theoretical Ideology of the Capitalist Economy
The Effective Reality of the Capitalist Economy
Relative Efficiency, Flexibility, and Resistance of Capitalism
scope_outcomes.criterion: Inventory definitions and actual uses of shared or salient terms, preserving distinct senses, negations, and local scope.
scope_outcomes.basis: The source explicitly defines and distinguishes rationality, instrumental rationality, economic rationality, rationalization, rational mastery, homo oeconomicus, and capitalist rationality, with anchored uses across the inspected sections.
limitations: Only one supplied work was available, so cross-work persistence or change cannot be assessed.
